html:
The Lipizzan is a horse breed developed at the stud farm of Lipica, in the Karst region of southwest Slovenia, founded in 1580 by Archduke Charles II of Habsburg.

The Habsburgs crossed Spanish horses with local and Arab stock to breed carriage and riding horses for the court. Lipizzans became the horses of the Spanish Riding School of Vienna, where they still perform classical dressage. The stud fled wars several times, and after World War I the herd was split between Austria and Italy. Lipica, then in Italy and later in Yugoslavia, is today in Slovenia, which put a pair of Lipizzans on its 20 cent euro coin.
sum: The Lipizzan is a horse breed developed at the stud farm of Lipica, in the Karst region of southwest Slovenia, founded in 1580 by Archduke Charles II of Habsburg.
